subject: DPA Annex: localized processing windows and transient log egress — operational checklist
messages:
From: Carl Jensen <carl.jensen@astracare.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@astracare.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: DPA Annex: localized processing windows and transient log egress — operational checklist

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we proceed to procurement, our security and legal teams need a short DPA annex to cover a few operational constraints specific to AstraCare. High-level asks: 

1) EU/localized processing default: all AstraCare production workloads serving EU patients must be processed and stored in EU regions by default.
2) Short-window transient egress: we can accept temporary cross-region processing only as a failover measure, limited to a maximum 36 hours per incident, with pre-notification to AstraCare Security whenever practical.
3) Subprocessor visibility: we need the current roster and confirmation that cache/CDN vendors do not persist PII outside the EU beyond the transient window.
4) Evidence: sample audit logs showing cross-region egress events, SFTP export stubs, and a sample key-wrapping flow.

Attached: AstraCare_DPA_Annex_Request_v1.pdf — this is the minimal annex our legal team will try to attach to the contract. Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to items 1–4, and if not, what the operational alternative is?

We'd like to keep timelines tight — procurement hopes to have a signed annex in two weeks.

Thanks,
Carl
Carl Jensen
Head of Security & Privacy
AstraCare


From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Carl Jensen <carl.jensen@astracare.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA Annex: localized processing windows and transient log egress — operational checklist

Carl — thanks for the clear ask and the annex draft. Short answers up front: we can meet the EU default and provide a constrained, auditable transient egress policy with some operational caveats. Below is a summary and proposed next steps.

Summary of commitments we can make today:
- EU-by-default: production tenant will be pinned to EU regions (data at rest + inference serving) for AstraCare; backups and logs also kept in EU by default.
- Transient egress: we can agree to an operational window of up to 48 hours for emergency failover (we are proposing 48h rather than 36h to allow for controlled remediation and system stabilization). During that window:
  * Egress is invoked only after automated local failover attempts fail and a runbook checklist is executed.
  * All egressed traffic is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest (AES-256).
  * Full audit trail: request IDs, origin/destination IPs, time-window, and a checksum of payloads will be recorded and made available via our secure S3 audit bucket for 90 days.
- KMS / key controls: we will use region-specific KMS keys (EU keys for AstraCare production) and will not export plaintext keys across regions.
- Subprocessor roster: we'll provide a current roster and flag any cache/CDN providers that perform ephemeral caching; we will exclude any subprocessor that persists PII outside the EU without a documented, customer-approved allowance.

Operational caveats / asks from AstraCare:
- Customer opt-in: the transient egress flow must be enabled per-tenant; we require AstraCare to formally opt-in via the annex (default is disabled).
- Coordination window: where possible, Redwood will provide a 2-hour pre-notice; in certain automated degraded-network incidents that is not viable.

Attachments I am adding: redwood_residency_operational_matrix.xlsx (operational mapping + proposed SLA language). Also opening a collaborative M-Plan doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Qf-Residency-MAP — please add your legal touch points.

Next steps:
1) Marissa — can you prepare the subprocessor CSV & minimal audit sample?
2) Jordan — can you scope the small addition to our DPA annex template (KMS clause + transient egress section)?
3) Carl — if AstraCare is OK with 48h instead of 36h we'll update the annex and circulate for DocuSign.

I'll follow up with a short Ops playbook in the next 24 hours.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference


From: Carl Jensen <carl.jensen@astracare.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, procure@astracare.com
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA Annex: localized processing windows and transient log egress — operational checklist

Vivek — thanks for the quick reply and for being explicit. A couple follow-ups from our side:

- 48h is acceptable if we get the following in the annex: automated notification to AstraCare Security on egress start, a commitment to no more than 3 transient egress incidents per calendar year without renegotiation, and an SLA to delete any transiently-stored payloads within 7 days post-incident unless our team requests retention for forensic purposes.
- Subprocessor question: you mentioned excluding subprocessors that persist PII outside the EU without approval — please explicitly confirm whether AnvilCache (an example vendor we track) is configured in a way that could persist content longer than ephemeral in non-EU nodes. We need a yes/no and short explanation.
- Evidence: our legal team would like a sample audit export (redacted) showing an egress event: include request-id, timestamps, source region, destination region, and S3 object path.

Attaching the AstraCare_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx — please have your security team fill sections 2 (processing locations) and 5 (subprocessors & retention).

Procurement is copied; once we have the annex language and the sample audit we can move to DocuSign.

Regards,
Carl


From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Carl Jensen <carl.jensen@astracare.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2027 10:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA Annex: localized processing windows and transient log egress — operational checklist

Carl — looping in the ops details you asked for and attaching our subprocessor roster.

Quick clarifications:
- AnvilCache (subprocessor id: AC-103) is used strictly for short-lived KV cache and edge-pop performance. It is configured to honor region affinity; by default their EU nodes keep TTLs <= 300s and do not write persistent snapshots to long-term storage. We have a standing contractual clause with them restricting PII persistence beyond ephemeral caches for customers with EU residency needs.

- Sample audit export (redacted): request-id 7f4a9c2b, start 2027-05-12T02:11:05Z, src-region: eu-west-1, dst-region: us-west-2, s3-path: s3://redwood-audit/eu-to-us/7f4a9c2b.json (redacted). We will provide a sanitized file via your secure SFTP — please provide an inbound SFTP user & key or we can share via a temporary pre-signed S3 link.

- Retention / deletion: ephemeral payloads written during transient egress are scheduled for automatic delete after 7 days. If AstraCare requests retention for investigation we will create a retention enclave with an extended TTL and record the authorization in the audit trail.

Attachment: subprocessor_roster_Q2_2027.csv (includes AnvilCache entry and per-subprocessor region policies).

Forwarding the draft runbook excerpt below for visibility:

---- Forwarded runbook excerpt ----
On failure of EU primary (health-check threshold breached), runtime triggers local retries (5 attempts). If retries fail and latency/availability thresholds remain unmet, the failover coordinator will: 
1) attempt warm-failover in EU secondary (if available);
2) if EU secondaries are exhausted, initiate controlled transient instance in nearest healthy region (US or APAC) — only with manual operator acknowledgement or if automation exceeds safety timeout;
3) mark all egressed objects with metadata 'transient-egress=true' and write audit record;
4) send automated notification to AstraCare_Security@astracare.com and to the tenant security contact.

---- end excerpt ----

I'll prepare the sanitized audit example and the inbound SFTP details by EOD Monday.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
Attachment: subprocessor_roster_Q2_2027.csv

- Please send the sanitized audit log sample to procure@astracare.com via SFTP. I'll open a procurement ticket once we receive the sanitized artifact and the updated annex language.
